 * reads from here. Keeping this in component-local state would scope the result
 * to whichever component ran the check, and the banner would never show.
 *
 * The Tauri `Update` handle itself is not serializable and stays in a
 * module-level ref inside `useUpdater`; only its displayable fields land here.
 *
 * Persistence: none. The downloaded package lives in the Rust resource table of
 * the current webview, so a pending update cannot outlive the process anyway.
 */

import type { StateCreator } from 'zustand'

/**
 * Phases of the update flow.
 *
 * - `idle`        nothing known, or the last attempt was abandoned
 * - `checking`    a manual check is in flight
 * - `downloading` package transfer in progress
 * - `scheduled`   package ready, waiting for the restart window
 * - `warning`     final countdown before the restart, user can act
 * - `installing`  handed to the installer; the process is about to die
 * - `error`       only ever reached from a user-initiated action
 */
export type UpdatePhase =
  | 'idle'
  | 'checking'
  | 'downloading'
  | 'scheduled'
  | 'warning'
  | 'installing'
  | 'error'

export interface UpdateInfo {
  version: string
  date: string | null
  body: string | null
}

/** Fields describing the pending update, reset together when it is abandoned. */
const CLEARED_FIELDS = {
  updatePhase: 'idle' as UpdatePhase,
  updateInfo: null as UpdateInfo | null,
  updateProgress: 0,
  updateRestartAt: null as number | null,
  updateSurfaced: false,
  updateError: null as string | null,
}

export const UPDATER_INITIAL_STATE = {
  ...CLEARED_FIELDS,
  updateAutoCheckStarted: false,
  updateFlowBusy: false,
}

export interface UpdaterSlice {
  // State
  updatePhase: UpdatePhase
  updateInfo: UpdateInfo | null
  updateProgress: number
  /** Epoch ms at which the app restarts, once one has been planned. */
  updateRestartAt: number | null
  /**
   * Whether the banner is on screen. The automatic hourly path downloads
   * without surfacing anything; startup, the final countdown and any
   * user-initiated action do surface.
   */
  updateSurfaced: boolean
  updateError: string | null
  /** Guards the app-wide automatic check loop against duplicate scheduling. */
  updateAutoCheckStarted: boolean
  /**
   * A check-and-download sequence is in flight. Phase alone cannot serialise
   * the manual and automatic paths: both start from `idle` and stay there
   * across their network round trip, so they would each claim the update.
   */
  updateFlowBusy: boolean

  // Actions
  setUpdateChecking: () => void
  setUpdateDownloading: (info: UpdateInfo, surfaced: boolean) => void
  setUpdateProgress: (progress: number) => void
  setUpdateScheduled: (restartAt: number) => void
  /** Put back a pending update whose replacement attempt came to nothing. */
  restoreScheduled: (info: UpdateInfo | null, restartAt: number, surfaced: boolean) => void
  setUpdateWarning: (restartAt: number) => void
  setUpdateInstalling: () => void
  setUpdateIdle: () => void
  setUpdateError: (error: string, surfaced: boolean) => void
  surfaceUpdate: () => void
  hideUpdateBanner: () => void
  markUpdateAutoCheckStarted: () => void
  setUpdateFlowBusy: (busy: boolean) => void
}

export const createUpdaterSlice: StateCreator<UpdaterSlice, [], [], UpdaterSlice> = (set) => ({
  ...UPDATER_INITIAL_STATE,

  setUpdateChecking: () => set({ updatePhase: 'checking', updateError: null }),

  setUpdateDownloading: (info, surfaced) =>
    set({
      updatePhase: 'downloading',
      updateInfo: info,
      updateProgress: 0,
      updateSurfaced: surfaced,
      updateError: null,
    }),

  setUpdateProgress: (progress) => set({ updateProgress: progress }),

  setUpdateScheduled: (restartAt) => set({ updatePhase: 'scheduled', updateRestartAt: restartAt }),

  restoreScheduled: (info, restartAt, surfaced) =>
    set({
      updatePhase: 'scheduled',
      updateInfo: info,
      updateRestartAt: restartAt,
      updateSurfaced: surfaced,
      updateProgress: 0,
      updateError: null,
    }),

  // The countdown is the one moment the user must not miss, so it surfaces
  // regardless of how the update was found.
  setUpdateWarning: (restartAt) =>
    set({ updatePhase: 'warning', updateRestartAt: restartAt, updateSurfaced: true }),

  setUpdateInstalling: () => set({ updatePhase: 'installing', updateSurfaced: true }),

  setUpdateIdle: () => set({ ...CLEARED_FIELDS }),

  // An automatic flow keeps its failures to the log, so `surfaced` is decided
  // by the caller rather than assumed here.
  setUpdateError: (error, surfaced) =>
    set({ updatePhase: 'error', updateSurfaced: surfaced, updateError: error, updateRestartAt: null }),

  surfaceUpdate: () => set({ updateSurfaced: true }),

  // Hides the banner without cancelling anything: the planned restart stands.
  hideUpdateBanner: () => set({ updateSurfaced: false }),

  markUpdateAutoCheckStarted: () => set({ updateAutoCheckStarted: true }),

  setUpdateFlowBusy: (busy) => set({ updateFlowBusy: busy }),
})
